title: Achaean League
capsule: The Achaean League was a federal confederation of Peloponnesian Greek city-states, refounded in 280 BCE after an initial Archaic precedent, that became the dominant political force in Greece during the Hellenistic period. Under Aratus of Sicyon (strategos repeatedly from 245 BCE) the league absorbed Corinth, Megara, and other major polities, presenting itself as the defender of Greek liberty against Macedonian domination and later Spartan aggression. The league defeated Cleomenes III of Sparta with Macedonian assistance at Sellasia in 222 BCE but subsequently fell into dependence on Rome, with growing internal tension over Roman interference. In 146 BCE the Roman general Lucius Mummius crushed the league forces at the Battle of Corinth, sacked Corinth, dissolved the confederation, and incorporated Greece into the Roman provincial system.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Member city-states of the league are well documented in ancient sources, but the precise territorial boundaries of league control fluctuated substantially with membership changes and military campaigns and cannot be mapped with precision.
